questions.q: What does a dictionary entry's Type attribute actually determine?
options: What the database column stores, how the form renders the field, and what further configuration becomes available
Only what color the field renders in on the form
Nothing — Type is a cosmetic label with no functional effect
Only whether the field appears in reports
questions.explain: Type is the most consequential choice on a dictionary entry — it drives storage, rendering, and available configuration like choice lists.

questions.q: What does a Reference field actually store, and how does Incident's caller_id use it?
options: The literal name of the caller as free text
The sys_id of a record on another table — caller_id references sys_user, the same way a foreign key would
A copy of every field from the related user record
Nothing; Reference fields are purely cosmetic lookups with no stored value
questions.explain: A Reference field stores the target record's sys_id, and the dictionary entry's Reference attribute names which table that sys_id points into.

questions.q: Why are Incident's Additional comments and Work notes fields built as Journal type rather than String?
options: Journal fields are just a cosmetic variant of String with no behavioral difference
String fields can't hold more than 40 characters
Journal fields are append-only, preserving every timestamped, attributed entry — which is what powers the Activity formatter's running history
Journal fields are required on every ServiceNow table by default
questions.explain: A String field would overwrite its previous value; Journal preserves every entry as its own timestamped record, which is exactly what Activity displays.

questions.q: What is a Glide List field, in relation to a Reference field?
options: A completely unrelated field type with no connection to References
A Reference field that can only ever point at the sys_user table
A type reserved exclusively for Date/Time fields
A multi-value cousin of Reference, storing a comma-separated set of sys_ids instead of just one
questions.explain: Glide List extends the same sys_id-pointer idea to multiple linked records at once, such as an Incident's Watch list.

questions.q: What problem do paired Document ID and Table Name fields solve?
options: Storing a currency amount alongside its currency code
Converting a timestamp to each viewer's personal time zone
Pointing at a record that could live on any of several different tables — the polymorphic reference problem a single ordinary Reference field can't handle
Rendering a Boolean field as a checkbox instead of a dropdown
questions.explain: Table Name stores which table the linked record lives on, and Document ID stores that record's sys_id — together resolving a reference a fixed-target Reference field type can't express.
